title: Covalently PD‐L1 Anchoring Drives Bispecific Nanostructure Assembly for Spatial Control of T Cell Recruitment and Activation
one_line: A two-component chemistry system oxidizes PD-L1's N-glycans on tumor cells to covalently nucleate self-assembling anti-CD3 peptide nanostructures that act as membrane-anchored BiTE mimics.
key_claims: The P1 probe (PD-L1-binding peptide, Kd ≈ 4.5 µM, conjugated to galactose oxidase) oxidizes C6 hydroxyls on PD-L1 N-glycans to aldehydes; oxidation was sharply reduced with the glycosylation-deficient 4NQ mutant (4 Asn→Gln), free galactose competition, and tunicamycin.

Covalent hydrazide–aldehyde anchoring of the self-assembling peptide (HSP) drops its critical aggregation concentration from 38.26 µM to 2.18 µM, driving β-sheet and π–π stacked artificial topological nanostructure (ATN) formation on the tumor surface.

In MDA-MB-231/primary T cell co-cultures, ATNs gave 2.61-fold higher tumor killing than non-assembling controls, roughly doubled IFN-γ secretion, and CD69 peaked at ~8 h; HCS imaging showed directional T cell migration and clustering at treated tumor cells.
In MC38 tumor-bearing mice (intratumoral P1, intravenous HSP), treatment achieved 62.6% tumor inhibition with increased intratumoral PD-1+ T cells and IFN-γ.

The covalent version outperformed a non-covalent analogue under mildly acidic, dynamic conditions, and efficacy extended to patient-derived lung cancer organoids (012T, 014T) with T cell infiltration.
limitations: Authors acknowledge risk of non-specific off-target glycan oxidation by galactose oxidase in a systemic context; TME-responsive activation is proposed for future work.
The PD-L1 targeting peptide has only micromolar affinity (4.5 µM), relying on covalent capture rather than high-affinity binding for retention.
In vivo delivery required local intratumoral administration of the P1 probe, not full systemic dosing.
No reported toxicity/biodistribution data in healthy tissues within the described material.
Anti-CD3 engagement bypasses antigen specificity, so on-target/off-tumor T cell activation if ATNs form elsewhere is untested.
open_questions: Does fully systemic administration of both components preserve tumor-restricted assembly and avoid healthy-tissue glycan oxidation?
Would a pH- or light/ultrasound-caged galactose oxidase deliver the same efficacy with a measurable safety margin?
How does ATN-mediated killing compare head-to-head with a conventional PD-L1 antibody plus a clinical BiTE?
Is efficacy dependent on PD-L1 expression level, and what threshold of surface PD-L1 is needed for assembly?
